newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh PM says privatisation to finish in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh PM says privatisation to finish in 1997.

text.p: Kazakhstan will finish the privatisation of state-owned industries, including gas pipelines, by 1997, Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said on Friday.
"State-owned properties have become catastrophically dangerous for the economy," Kazhegeldin told reporters following a meeting of representatives from donor countries in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
Kazhegeldin said tenders had already been opened for the oil-rich Central Asian nation's electricity industry.
Belgium's Tractebel bought Almaty's municipal power company, Almatyenergo, in August for $340 million.
He added the gas pipeline networks of GAO Kazakhgaz, Alaugaz and other regional gas transport entities would be privatised.
Kazhegeldin said the former Soviet republic was anxious for foreign participation in the tenders as cash constraints on Kazakh firms would draw out the privatisation process.
He said foreign consultants from Banque Paribas, Merrill Lynch investment bank, accountants Price Waterhouse and other firms would make the tender process transparent.
Many foreign investors complain privately that privatisation rules in Kazakhstan are unclear. But there is large interest in the republic's substantial oil, gas and mineral reserves.
